To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a new solid-phase inhibition assay was developed for the binding of von Willebrand Factor (vWF) with GPIb, and this new assay was shown to be as sensitive and reliable as the conventional liquid-phase inhibition assay.
we developed a new assay to study the binding of von Willebrand Factor (vWF) and platelet glycoproteins, which is a convenient alternative for the conventional assay using 125-I-vWF.

the binding of biologically active von Willebrand Factor (vWF) fragments to platelet GPIb was inhibited by monoclonal antibody to GPIb, monoclonal antibody against vWF, and two vWF peptides that contain vWF's putatively active site for GPIb.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of inhibitors of vWF binding to platelet GPIb, which may prove to be useful in the treatment of bleeding disorders associated with a deficiency of vWF.
the development of a new solid-phase assay to detect inhibitors of the binding between vWF and GPIb.
a new assay for vWF binding to GPIb in which the platelets are bound to the microplate via the anti-GP IIb/IIIa mAb VNR-5 in the presence of either ristocetin, botrocetin, or both.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the solid-phase inhibition assay using biotinylabeled vWF is useful and convenient for screening inhibitors for the binding of vWf to GPIb in the presence of either ristocetin and/or botrocetin.
this assay is a useful and convenient tool for the study of GPIb-vWF interactions and that it is applicable to the analysis of other platelet glycoproteins.
this new assay is useful in the screening of GPIb-binding inhibitors and in the characterization of GPIb-binding domains on vWF.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a solid-phase ELISA with platelet-bound GPIIb/IIIb and GPIIb/IX as the immobilized platelet receptors.
this assay is a useful tool for the screening of inhibitors of the vWF/GPIb interaction and the study of the structure-function relationship of the vWF molecule.
this solid-phase inhibition assay is a convenient, sensitive, and rapid method to study vWF's interaction with GPIb.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we developed a solid-phase assay for the binding inhibition assay of biotin-vWF to GPIb in the presence of either ristocetin and botrocetin.

the binding assay for vWF to platelet-bound wells in the presence and absence of the GPIb ligands ristocetin and botrocetin, respectively, is an effective tool for the study of the vWF-binding domain of vWF.
the solid-phase inhibition assay is a convenient and rapid alternative to the conventional liquid-phase inhibition assay.
